title: Turkey’s President Fights for Political Survival

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼带来的《重塑者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Skyrocketing inflation and a devastating earthquake left Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan vulnerable at the ballot box for the first time in his 20 years in power.
sentences.zh: 飙升的通货膨胀和一场毁灭性的地震，让土耳其总统雷杰普·塔伊普·埃尔多安在他执政20年来首次在投票箱前感到岌岌可危。
zh_words: 雷杰普·塔伊普·埃尔多安

sentences.en: In an election over the weekend, he was forced to a runoff, the first in Turkey's history.
sentences.zh: 在上周末的选举中，他被迫进入决选，这是土耳其历史上的第一次。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Ben Hubbard on Erdogan's fight for political survival and what it says about democracy in Turkey.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事本·哈伯德将讲述埃尔多安的政治生存之战，以及这对于土耳其民主意味着什么。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, May 17th.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月17日，星期三。

sentences.en: So Ben, Turkey just had an election over the weekend where the country's leader, Recep Tayyip Erdogan, failed to clear the hurdle to win outright.
sentences.zh: 那么本，土耳其刚在上周末举行了选举，该国领导人雷杰普·塔伊普·埃尔多安未能达到直接胜出的门槛。

sentences.en: And now the country's headed to a runoff.
sentences.zh: 现在该国即将进入决选。

sentences.en: Help us understand what this means.
sentences.zh: 请帮我们解读一下这意味着什么。

sentences.en: I mean, this was really a remarkable moment in modern Turkish history and in the history of Erdogan,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这确实是现代土耳其历史以及埃尔多安个人历史上一个非凡的时刻，

sentences.en: who has been by far the dominant politician on the national stage here for the last 20 years.
sentences.zh: 他在过去20年里一直是土耳其政坛绝对的主导者。

sentences.en: Going into the vote on Sunday, he was down in the polls, which he has never been before.
sentences.zh: 在周日的投票前，他的民调支持率下滑，这是他从未经历过的。

sentences.en: And he went into the election and he lost support in districts across the country, had fewer people voting for him.
sentences.zh: 他参加了选举，但在全国各地的选区支持率都有所下降，投他票的人变少了。

sentences.en: And he failed to get more than 50 percent of the vote, which would have automatically given him a third presidential term.
sentences.zh: 他未能获得超过50%的选票，否则他本可以直接获得第三个总统任期。

sentences.en: But if you look at this another way, it's not a setback at all.
sentences.zh: 但如果换个角度看，这根本算不上挫折。

sentences.en: He's still in this race, and this is really the latest chapter in the longer Erdogan story, which is one of a politician of incredible talents who has just repeatedly,
sentences.zh: 他依然在竞争中，这实际上是埃尔多安漫长故事的最新篇章，这个故事讲述了一位才华横溢的政治家如何一次又一次地，

sentences.en: against the odds, managed to keep himself on top.
sentences.zh: 在逆境中成功保住了自己的地位。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, I covered Turkey for four years, and I just remember Erdogan as this astute, savvy force that was just absolutely dominant in Turkish politics.
sentences.zh: 我曾报道过土耳其四年，我记忆中的埃尔多安是一位精明、老练的政治力量，在土耳其政坛拥有绝对的统治力。

sentences.en: So, let's talk about that then.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们来谈谈这个吧。

sentences.en: Where does the story of Erdogan as political survivor begin?
sentences.zh: 埃尔多安作为“政治幸存者”的故事是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: Before Erdogan came along, Turkish politics tended to be dominated by elites in the big cities, very much steeped in this idea that even though it's a Muslim-majority society,
sentences.zh: 在埃尔多安出现之前，土耳其政坛往往由大城市的精英阶层主导，他们深受一种观念影响：尽管这是一个穆斯林占多数的社会，

sentences.en: that it was a staunchly secular place.
sentences.zh: 但它必须是一个坚定的世俗国家。

sentences.en: But Erdogan comes up on a completely different track.
sentences.zh: 但埃尔多安走的是一条完全不同的道路。

sentences.en: He's not from the elite.
sentences.zh: 他并非出身精英阶层。

sentences.en: He grew up in a poor, tough neighborhood in Istanbul.
sentences.zh: 他在伊斯坦布尔一个贫穷且环境恶劣的社区长大。

sentences.en: He attended religious schools, which at the time were supposed to be only for people who wanted to become preachers and serve in other religious functions.
sentences.zh: 他上的是宗教学校，当时这些学校被认为只适合那些想成为传教士并从事其他宗教工作的人。

sentences.en: And then he got into politics.
sentences.zh: 后来他投身政坛。

sentences.en: He serves a stint as the mayor of Istanbul in the 90s and is celebrated all around.
sentences.zh: 他在90年代担任过伊斯坦布尔市长，并广受赞誉。

sentences.en: People give him a lot of credit for organizing what was otherwise a polluted and messy, gigantic metropolis.
sentences.zh: 人们非常认可他治理这座原本污染严重、混乱不堪的巨大都市的能力。

sentences.en: And then he gets his first shot at the national stage.
sentences.zh: 随后，他获得了第一次登上全国舞台的机会。

sentences.en: In 2002, his party, which he had just helped found, comes out of nowhere and wins a majority in the parliament.
sentences.zh: 2002年，他参与创立的政党异军突起，赢得了议会多数席位。

sentences.en: And this is basically a protest vote by Turks who were so angry at the way that the previous parties had been running the country that they decide to give these guys a chance.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是土耳其民众的一次抗议投票，他们对前几届政府治理国家的方式感到愤怒，于是决定给这些人一个机会。

sentences.en: And the year after that, 2003, Erdogan is able to get himself into parliament and promptly becomes the prime minister.
sentences.zh: 第二年，即2003年，埃尔多安成功进入议会，并迅速成为总理。

sentences.en: So he comes in and all of a sudden he's basically in charge of the government.
sentences.zh: 所以他一上台，就立刻掌握了政府大权。

sentences.en: And the country has really never seen anything like this.
sentences.zh: 这个国家此前从未见过这样的情况。

sentences.en: He's a scrappy underdog.
sentences.zh: 他是一个不屈不挠的挑战者。

sentences.en: He's largely representative of a large religious underclass in the country.
sentences.zh: 他在很大程度上代表了国内庞大的宗教底层阶级。

sentences.en: People who tend to be devout, who felt for a long time like they were looked down upon by the urban elites.
sentences.zh: 这些人往往虔诚，长期以来感觉被城市精英所轻视。

sentences.en: We're talking about the poorer parts of society.
sentences.zh: 我们指的是社会中较贫困的部分。

sentences.en: And they rally around him and they see him as their champion.
sentences.zh: 他们团结在他周围，视他为自己的捍卫者。

sentences.en: And then Turkey really takes off.
sentences.zh: 随后，土耳其真正腾飞了。

sentences.en: During his first decade as the prime minister, Turkey's GDP more than tripled.
sentences.zh: 在他担任总理的第一个十年里，土耳其的GDP增长了两倍多。

sentences.en: He went about a building spree, basically, where new neighborhoods, new areas, new homes cropped up across the country.
sentences.zh: 他开启了一场建设狂潮，全国各地涌现出新的社区、新的区域和新的住宅。

sentences.en: They built new hospitals.
sentences.zh: 他们建造了新的医院。

sentences.en: They built airports in lots of the regional cities, highways, rail lines.
sentences.zh: 他们在许多区域性城市修建了机场、高速公路和铁路线。

sentences.en: And so for people living in Turkey,
sentences.zh: 因此，对于生活在土耳其的人们来说，

sentences.en: the country really goes from a place where a lot of people are poor and don't have great services to a place where a lot of people are middle class and can really take advantage of it.
sentences.zh: 这个国家确实从一个许多人贫穷且缺乏优质服务的地方，变成了一个许多人步入中产阶级并能真正从中受益的地方。

sentences.en: People are buying homes.
sentences.zh: 人们开始买房。

sentences.en: They're buying cars.
sentences.zh: 他们开始买车。

sentences.en: They're earning more money.
sentences.zh: 他们的收入增加了。

sentences.en: And so he, you know, was tremendously popular for that.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他因此获得了巨大的声望。

sentences.en: And voters continue to reward him and his party at the ballot box.
sentences.zh: 选民们在投票箱前不断地奖励他和他的政党。

sentences.en: I mean, this was a revolution in Turkish politics.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是土耳其政坛的一场革命。

sentences.en: I mean, this was not typical for a Turkish leader and people really loved him for it.
sentences.zh: 这在土耳其领导人中并不典型，人们确实因此非常爱戴他。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But then after his first decade in power, the sheen starts to come off.
sentences.zh: 但执政十年后，光环开始褪去。

sentences.en: We enter sort of a new chapter in the history of Erdogan where we really see new efforts to squeeze any kind of dissent or opposition to his rule to consolidate his control over the states.
sentences.zh: 我们进入了埃尔多安历史的新篇章，我们看到他采取了新的手段来压制任何异见或反对声音，以巩固他对国家的控制。

sentences.en: It starts with pressure on journalists, pressure on the opposition, efforts to modify the government.
sentences.zh: 这始于对记者和反对派的压力，以及修改政府结构的尝试。

sentences.en: And these really gets turbocharged after an attempted coup against him in 2016.
sentences.zh: 在2016年针对他的一次未遂政变后，这些手段变得更加激进。

sentences.en: The Turkish military says in a statement that it has taken control of the country and imposed martial law.
sentences.zh: 土耳其军方发表声明称，已控制国家并实施戒严。

sentences.en: It's carried out by a religious group that had previously been close allies and people in the military.
sentences.zh: 政变是由一个此前曾是亲密盟友的宗教团体和军方人员实施的。

sentences.en: And they literally try to overthrow the government.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至试图推翻政府。

sentences.en: Erdogan is at a vacation retreat.
sentences.zh: 当时埃尔多安正在度假。

sentences.en: They send commandos in to try to kidnap him.
sentences.zh: 他们派遣突击队试图绑架他。

sentences.en: He gets wind of it and gets out of there before they arrive.
sentences.zh: 他提前得到消息，在他们到达之前就离开了。

sentences.en: I mean, it's like something out of an action movie.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直就像动作电影里的情节。

sentences.en: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan speaking to the country via a FaceTime call into CNN Turk, telling his supporters to go to the streets to fight for democracy.
sentences.zh: 土耳其总统雷杰普·塔伊普·埃尔多安通过FaceTime连线CNN土耳其频道向全国发表讲话，呼吁支持者走上街头为民主而战。
zh_words: 雷杰普·塔伊普·埃尔多安

sentences.en: But then he survives.
sentences.zh: 但他活了下来。

sentences.en: Well, the attempted coup on the Turkish government is seen to have increased public backing for the president, with several thousand people in Istanbul rallying in his support.
sentences.zh: 嗯，针对土耳其政府的未遂政变被认为反而增加了公众对总统的支持，数千人在伊斯坦布尔集会支持他。

sentences.en: And he really takes advantage of this coup and uses it to further consolidate his power.
sentences.zh: 他确实利用了这次政变，并借此进一步巩固了自己的权力。

sentences.en: Altogether, more than 50,000 people have either been sacked or suspended since the coup attempt, including police, judges, soldiers and generals.
sentences.zh: 政变未遂后，总共有超过5万人被解雇或停职，包括警察、法官、士兵和将军。

sentences.en: Tens of thousands of people are arrested, are purged from their jobs in the government bureaucracy, in the judiciary, in other parts of the state.
sentences.zh: 数万人被捕，并从政府官僚机构、司法部门和国家其他部门的职位上被清洗。

sentences.en: The education ministry suspended over 15,000 personnel.
sentences.zh: 教育部停职了超过1.5万名员工。

sentences.en: We can make comparison between the Makartya era and Turkey right now.
sentences.zh: 我们可以把现在的土耳其与麦卡锡时代做个比较。

sentences.en: And many of these people are replaced by loyalists, by people who belong to his party.
sentences.zh: 这些人中的许多被忠诚者，也就是他政党的人所取代。

sentences.en: And that gives him even more sway over the government.
sentences.zh: 这使他对政府拥有了更大的掌控力。

sentences.en: And mark this the day that Turkey changed forever.
sentences.zh: 记住这一天，土耳其从此改变了。

sentences.en: Thousands celebrate a new constitution.
sentences.zh: 数千人庆祝新宪法。

sentences.en: In 2017, he backs a referendum that passes by a slim margin, but passes...
sentences.zh: 2017年，他支持的一项公投以微弱优势通过，但毕竟通过了……

sentences.en: It would completely change the political system here from a parliamentary to a presidential republic.
sentences.zh: 这将把这里的政治体制从议会制彻底转变为总统制共和国。

sentences.en: Mr. Erdogan would have vastly enhanced powers.
sentences.zh: 埃尔多安先生将拥有大幅增强的权力。

sentences.en: The prime minister would be scrapped.
sentences.zh: 总理职位将被取消。

sentences.en: And of course, he at the time is the president.
sentences.zh: 当然，他当时就是总统。

sentences.en: So while his own allies say this is just like an American or a French or a South Korean presidential system, in fact, it's not really.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管他自己的盟友说这就像美国、法国或韩国的总统制，但实际上并非如此。

sentences.en: He can, for instance, appoint the majority of the main judges, 12 out of 15.
sentences.zh: 例如，他可以任命主要法官中的大多数，即15人中的12人。

sentences.en: And so this gives him even more powers than he had before.
sentences.zh: 这使他比以前拥有了更大的权力。

sentences.en: And he takes those powers and uses them to give himself even more powers.
sentences.zh: 他利用这些权力，又为自己争取了更多的权力。

sentences.en: And so this is really when we head into the area where people start worrying about the health of Turkish democracy
sentences.zh: 所以，这确实是我们进入人们开始担心土耳其民主健康状况的阶段，

sentences.en: and wondering how far is it going to tip from democracy towards authoritarianism.
sentences.zh: 并怀疑它会从民主向威权主义倾斜到什么程度。

sentences.en: And is he really out to establish a system of one-man rule?
sentences.zh: 他是否真的要建立一个一人统治的体制？

sentences.en: And of course, all along the way, he's still winning open elections, right?
sentences.zh: 当然，一路走来，他一直在赢得公开选举，对吧？

sentences.en: And handily.
sentences.zh: 而且赢得轻而易举。

sentences.en: And this is the challenge.
sentences.zh: 这就是挑战所在。

sentences.en: And frankly, this is what he and his supporters will always say is like, why are you talking about autocracy?
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，这就是他和他的支持者总是会说的：你们为什么要谈论独裁？

sentences.en: The guy keeps winning elections.
sentences.zh: 这家伙一直在赢得选举。

sentences.en: I mean, in the most recent presidential elections before this one in 2018, he won in the first round with about 52%.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在2018年这次选举之前的最近一次总统选举中，他在第一轮就以约52%的得票率获胜。

sentences.en: His nearest challenger was more than 20 points behind him.
sentences.zh: 他最接近的挑战者落后他20多个百分点。

sentences.en: So, you know, his defenders will say, what are you complaining about?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他的辩护者会说，你们在抱怨什么？

sentences.en: The people have spoken and they have chosen Erdogan yet again.
sentences.zh: 人民已经发声，他们再次选择了埃尔多安。

sentences.en: So why are you complaining?
sentences.zh: 所以你们为什么要抱怨？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: But that same year, Erdogan faces a new threat that really strikes directly at his popularity among voters.
sentences.zh: 但就在同一年，埃尔多安面临了一个新的威胁，这直接打击了他在选民中的人气。

sentences.en: Turkey's central bank has confirmed what consumers have already learned the hard way.
sentences.zh: 土耳其央行证实了消费者已经亲身体会到的事实。

sentences.en: It's predicting inflation will hit a 15-year high this year.
sentences.zh: 预计今年通胀率将达到15年来的最高点。

sentences.en: The currency starts losing its value and prices start to go up.
sentences.zh: 货币开始贬值，物价开始上涨。

sentences.en: Food prices shot up by 34% in the third quarter.
sentences.zh: 第三季度食品价格飙升了34%。

sentences.en: And all the money spent on essentials meant fewer purchases of white goods, cars, and other big-ticket iteMs.
sentences.zh: 所有花在生活必需品上的钱，意味着购买白色家电、汽车和其他大件商品的支出减少了。

sentences.en: And that means basically that people's money is not worth what it used to be worth.
sentences.zh: 这意味着人们手中的钱不再值钱了。

sentences.en: They can't buy the same things that they used to buy.
sentences.zh: 他们买不到以前能买到的东西了。

sentences.en: Their salaries are just worth less.
sentences.zh: 他们的工资缩水了。

sentences.en: And in one sense, this is very much the culmination of these years of economic policy, of massive government spending, lots of it built on debt.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这正是多年经济政策的必然结果，即大规模的政府支出，其中许多是建立在债务之上的。

sentences.en: And these were policies that he championed and that he was largely in charge of.
sentences.zh: 这些政策是他所倡导的，他也在很大程度上负责这些政策。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Basically, to grow Turkey, as we talked about earlier, he pursued this single-minded approach to the economy, which kind of amounted to pouring sugar water into it.
sentences.zh: 基本上，为了发展土耳其，正如我们之前谈到的，他采取了一种单一的经济方针，这相当于往里面倒糖水。

sentences.en: Like, it was intended for rapid growth, which he succeeded at.
sentences.zh: 就像是为了快速增长，他也确实成功了。

sentences.en: But at some point, as we all know, when the sugar runs out, you get a headache.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们所知，当糖分耗尽时，你就会头疼。

sentences.en: This is very much the end of the sugar high.
sentences.zh: 这正是“糖分兴奋”的终结。

sentences.en: Prices keep going up and they keep going up.
sentences.zh: 物价一直在上涨，而且还在不断上涨。

sentences.en: And Erdogan basically makes it worse.
sentences.zh: 而埃尔多安基本上让情况变得更糟了。

sentences.en: Erdogan calls himself an enemy of interest rates.
sentences.zh: 埃尔多安自称是利率的敌人。

sentences.en: He says they lead to inflation, though the opposite has been proven true.
sentences.zh: 他说利率会导致通货膨胀，尽管事实证明恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Most economists will tell you that if you have an inflation problem, the first thing that you should do is raise interest rates to try to cool off the economy.
sentences.zh: 大多数经济学家会告诉你，如果你有通胀问题，你应该做的第一件事就是提高利率，试图让经济降温。

sentences.en: He does exactly the opposite, and he starts reducing them.
sentences.zh: 他却反其道而行之，开始降息。

sentences.en: He reduces interest rates.
sentences.zh: 他降低了利率。

sentences.en: Yes, repeatedly.
sentences.zh: 是的，反复降息。

sentences.en: Man, when are we going to be wise?
sentences.zh: 天哪，我们什么时候才能变得明智？

sentences.en: You can control the interest rates, but you cannot control inflation.
sentences.zh: 你可以控制利率，但你无法控制通货膨胀。

sentences.en: Inflation occurs as a result of your wrong steps.
sentences.zh: 通货膨胀是你错误决策的结果。

sentences.en: And who pays the price?
sentences.zh: 谁来买单？

sentences.en: Our people above all.
sentences.zh: 首先是我们的人民。

sentences.en: At the same time, he is sort of burning through central bank chiefs.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他一直在频繁更换央行行长。

sentences.en: He numerous times fires the central bank chief and brings in somebody else.
sentences.zh: 他多次解雇央行行长，然后换上另一个人。

sentences.en: Turkey's President Erdogan shook markets again by replacing the head of his central bank again, this time after just four months on the job.
sentences.zh: 土耳其总统埃尔多安再次更换央行行长，震惊了市场，这次距离上一任上任仅四个月。

sentences.en: And through that process, we really see that, you know, he's in charge.
sentences.zh: 通过这个过程，我们确实看到，你知道，他在掌控一切。

sentences.en: He's running the show.
sentences.zh: 他在主导全局。

sentences.en: He's the one who's setting the policy.
sentences.zh: 他是制定政策的人。

sentences.en: Mr. Atbal's successor, Shahab Kabjoglu, falls more in line with President Erdogan's unorthodox thinking about interest rates and inflation.
sentences.zh: 阿格巴尔的继任者沙哈普·卡夫哲奥卢，在利率和通胀问题上更符合埃尔多安总统非传统的思维方式。

sentences.en: This builds and builds and builds until late last year when inflation shoots above 80 percent.
sentences.zh: 这种情况不断累积，直到去年年底，通胀率飙升至80%以上。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Inflation in Turkey jumped to a 24-year high one week after the central bank cut interest rates again.
sentences.zh: 在央行再次降息一周后，土耳其的通胀率跃升至24年来的最高点。

sentences.en: I mean, by comparison, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，相比之下，美国去年通胀率的峰值是9%。

sentences.en: peak was 9 percent last year.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，80%简直令人难以置信。

sentences.en: I mean, 80 percent is just unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 然而，一家独立的通胀研究机构声称，实际通胀率高达186%。

sentences.en: ...agency, however, an independent inflation research group claims that the actual rate stands at a whopping 186 percent.
sentences.zh: 随着国家面对雷杰普·塔伊普·埃尔多安总统违背广泛认可的通胀常识的非传统经济方针，里拉正处于自由落体状态。
zh_words: 雷杰普·塔伊普·埃尔多安

sentences.en: The lira is in freefall as the country reckons with President Rajep Tayyip Erdogan's unorthodox economic approach, which is contrary to widely accepted inflationary wisdom.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你甚至该怎么去杂货店列购物清单呢？

sentences.en: I mean, how do you even go to the grocery store and plan a grocery list?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你甚至该怎么去杂货店列购物清单呢？

sentences.en: It really undermines sort of anybody on any kind of a fixed income, whether you're retired and you're getting a pension, whether you're a teacher, whether you're a bus driver.
sentences.zh: 这确实削弱了任何靠固定收入生活的人，无论是退休领养老金的，还是教师，亦或是公交车司机。

sentences.en: Turkey is in economic turmoil.
sentences.zh: 土耳其正处于经济动荡之中。

sentences.en: People are queuing for bread, cutting back on meat, and are even fleeing to other countries.
sentences.zh: 人们排队买面包，减少肉类消费，甚至有人逃往其他国家。

sentences.en: Prices are high.
sentences.zh: 物价高涨。

sentences.en: We're really struggling.
sentences.zh: 我们真的在苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: We have two children who go to school.
sentences.zh: 我们有两个孩子在上学。

sentences.en: We are only earning minimum wage, and it's hard to make a living.
sentences.zh: 我们只拿最低工资，很难维持生计。

sentences.en: You're just basically watching your salary effectively get smaller and smaller and smaller,
sentences.zh: 你基本上只能眼睁睁看着自己的工资变得越来越少，越来越少，

sentences.en: and every time you go to the grocery store, you see that the prices for onions or tomatoes or pasta or rice
sentences.zh: 每次去杂货店，你都会发现洋葱、西红柿、意大利面或大米的价格，

sentences.en: or anything that you might want to buy just sort of going off the charts.
sentences.zh: 或者任何你想买的东西，价格都在飞涨。

sentences.en: And so it changes the way that people eat.
sentences.zh: 所以这改变了人们的饮食方式。

sentences.en: It changes the kind of trips that they take.
sentences.zh: 它改变了人们的出行方式。

sentences.en: It changes how much they drive, because people just have to cut things out of their budget that they can't afford anymore.
sentences.zh: 它改变了人们的开车频率，因为人们不得不从预算中剔除那些他们再也负担不起的东西。

sentences.en: You know, this is the definition of a pocketbook issue, and it's really just hitting people all the way across the country.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是典型的“钱袋子”问题，它确实在全国范围内影响着每一个人。

sentences.en: I don't see a future here.
sentences.zh: 我在这里看不到未来。

sentences.en: I actually want to go abroad.
sentences.zh: 我其实想出国。

sentences.en: This is true for most of us.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人都是这样。

sentences.en: That really opens up a new possibility for something unusual to happen.
sentences.zh: 这确实为发生不同寻常的事情开启了新的可能性。

sentences.en: So in the lead-up to this year's presidential election, we have the historically fractured Turkish opposition coalesce.
sentences.zh: 因此，在今年总统大选前夕，我们看到历史上四分五裂的土耳其反对派联合了起来。

sentences.en: They come together, a group of six opposition parties whose ideologies are quite diverse, and there's many things they don't agree on.
sentences.zh: 他们走到了一起，这是一个由六个意识形态迥异的反对党组成的联盟，他们之间有很多分歧。

sentences.en: They come together as a coalition and back a common presidential candidate.
sentences.zh: 他们结成联盟，共同支持一位总统候选人。

sentences.en: So as we get into this year, we're in this very unique position where we have people suffering because of the economy.
sentences.zh: 所以进入今年，我们处于一个非常独特的境地，人们正因经济问题而受苦。

sentences.en: We have a united Turkish opposition.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有一个团结的土耳其反对派。

sentences.en: And so Erdogan starts heading towards this election, facing a political threat in the one place that he's always been strongeSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，埃尔多安在走向这场选举时，在他一直以来最强大的地方感受到了政治威胁。

sentences.en: Which is at the ballot box.
sentences.zh: 那就是投票箱。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning, and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空探索七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟中最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 庆祝175年来帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受 nytimes.com/subscribe 的特别优惠。

sentences.en: So Ben, tell me about this opposition coalition and the candidate they decided to back.
sentences.zh: 那么本，跟我说说这个反对派联盟以及他们决定支持的候选人吧。

sentences.en: Who is he and what is his pitch to Turkish voters?
sentences.zh: 他是谁？他向土耳其选民提出了什么主张？

sentences.en: So the coalition has come together behind a man named Kamal Kalistaroulu.
sentences.zh: 这个联盟支持的是一个叫凯末尔·克勒奇达尔奥卢的人。

sentences.en: He is the head of the largest opposition party that the coalition is sort of built around, and he's a former civil servant.
sentences.zh: 他是该联盟所围绕的最大反对党的领导人，曾是一名公务员。

sentences.en: Basically worked his entire career in the government, and his last job was running the equivalent of the Social Security Administration.
sentences.zh: 他基本上整个职业生涯都在政府工作，最后一份工作是管理相当于社会保障局的机构。

sentences.en: And what's he like?
sentences.zh: 他是个什么样的人？

sentences.en: I mean, what's his pitch?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他的主张是什么？

sentences.en: He's almost the polar opposite of Erdogan.
sentences.zh: 他几乎是埃尔多安的对立面。

sentences.en: He's someone who's seen to be somewhat quiet, somewhat reasonable in his way of discussing things, very modest in how he presents himself to voters.
sentences.zh: 他被认为是一个比较安静、讨论问题时比较理性、在选民面前表现得非常谦逊的人。

sentences.en: I mean, I think the biggest indication of this are these videos that he's released throughout the campaign of him sitting in his kitchen.
sentences.zh: 我认为最能说明这一点的是他在竞选期间发布的那些坐在厨房里的视频。

sentences.en: It's a very modest Turkish kitchen, like you would see, you know, in most middle-class families, somewhat old-fashioned.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常朴素的土耳其厨房，就像你在大多数中产阶级家庭看到的那样，有点过时。

sentences.en: There's some tea towels hanging behind him on the oven.
sentences.zh: 他身后的烤箱上挂着几条茶巾。

sentences.en: And people noticed in one of the recent videos that it looks like he had bought a new air fryer.
sentences.zh: 人们注意到在最近的一个视频中，他好像买了一个新的空气炸锅。

sentences.en: And he literally just sits at the table and talks about stuff.
sentences.zh: 他真的只是坐在桌子旁谈论事情。

sentences.en: You know, he did one recently where he had an onion as a prop.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他最近做了一个视频，用洋葱作为道具。

sentences.en: An onion?
sentences.zh: 洋葱？

sentences.en: Yeah, he held up the onion, which people use often in their cooking, and talked about how expensive they had become to go after Erdogan and his party
sentences.zh: 是的，他举起人们做饭常用的洋葱，谈论它们变得有多贵，以此来抨击埃尔多安及其政党，

sentences.en: and really hit them hard with this inflation problem.
sentences.zh: 并用通货膨胀问题狠狠地打击他们。

sentences.en: And he says, look, this is our actual agenda.
sentences.zh: 他说，看，这就是我们真正的议程。

sentences.en: They know that when I come to power, democracy will come, money will flow, and your purchasing power will increase.
sentences.zh: 他们知道，当我上台后，民主就会到来，资金就会流动，你们的购买力就会提高。

sentences.en: They have no shame.
sentences.zh: 他们真无耻。

sentences.en: So Erdogan is in this very unfamiliar situation, right?
sentences.zh: 所以埃尔多安现在处于一个非常陌生的境地，对吧？

sentences.en: Where he's facing a real opposition that has a serious chance of beating him.
sentences.zh: 他面临着一个有很大机会击败他的真正反对派。

sentences.en: So what does he do?
sentences.zh: 那么他做了什么？

sentences.en: He goes on the attack.
sentences.zh: 他发起了攻击。

sentences.en: He runs a very aggressive campaign against Kılıçdaroğlu.
sentences.zh: 他对克勒奇达尔奥卢发动了非常激进的竞选活动。

sentences.en: He many times appears quite angry in his public appearances.
sentences.zh: 他在公开露面时多次表现得非常愤怒。

sentences.en: He belittles him.
sentences.zh: 他贬低他。

sentences.en: He at one point refers to him as a drunkard.
sentences.zh: 他一度称他为酒鬼。

sentences.en: A drunkard?
sentences.zh: 酒鬼？

sentences.en: Well, it's kind of a way to code to more religious voters that this guy is secular.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一种向更虔诚的选民暗示这家伙是世俗派的方式。

sentences.en: And so he's not the kind of person that you're looking for.
sentences.zh: 所以他不是你想要的那种人。

sentences.en: He's not from the religious class that we are type thing.
sentences.zh: 他不是我们那种宗教阶层的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's very much a code for he's not one of us or sort of the religious parts of society.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上是一种暗语，意思是“他不是我们自己人”或者不是社会中宗教群体的一员。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he tries to create this general image of this is somebody who is incompetent and incapable and weak.
sentences.zh: 他试图营造一种普遍形象，即这是一个无能、软弱的人。

sentences.en: And if you elect him as your president,
sentences.zh: 如果你选他当总统，

sentences.en: Turkey's going to be in a lot of trouble.
sentences.zh: 土耳其就会陷入大麻烦。

sentences.en: So that's what he says.
sentences.zh: 这就是他所说的。

sentences.en: What does he do during the campaign, Ben?
sentences.zh: 他在竞选期间做了什么，本？

sentences.en: Well, at the same time, he basically taps this tremendous power that he has as the president in this powerful presidential system.
sentences.zh: 嗯，与此同时，他基本上利用了他在这个强大的总统制体系中作为总统所拥有的巨大权力。

sentences.en: And uses the resources of the state to boost his chances in the campaign.
sentences.zh: 并利用国家资源来增加他在竞选中的胜算。

sentences.en: And so he, three times in the last year and a half, has raised the minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年半里，他三次提高了最低工资。

sentences.en: He raises pay for civil servants.
sentences.zh: 他提高了公务员的工资。

sentences.en: He changes some of the regulations about pensions to allow millions of Turks to get their pension early.
sentences.zh: 他修改了一些养老金法规，允许数百万土耳其人提前领取养老金。

sentences.en: A few weeks ago, we were in one of the medium-sized towns in the middle of the country.
sentences.zh: 几周前，我们在中部地区的一个中等城市。

sentences.en: And we met a guy who's so excited because he's about to get his pension at age 46.
sentences.zh: 我们遇到一个人，他非常兴奋，因为他46岁就要领养老金了。

sentences.en: And that's all because of these regulations that Erdogan has changed.
sentences.zh: 这完全是因为埃尔多安修改了这些规定。

sentences.en: His ability to do these things is so unchecked that he can just basically open the tap of public spending and pour money onto these people to protect them in the short term
sentences.zh: 他做这些事的能力不受制约，以至于他基本上可以打开公共支出的水龙头，向这些人倾注资金，以在短期内保护他们，

sentences.en: from the very painful effects of this inflation that we've been talking about.
sentences.zh: 免受我们一直在谈论的这种痛苦的通货膨胀的影响。

sentences.en: But in the long term, the bills are eventually going to come due and somebody's going to have to figure out how to cover them.
sentences.zh: 但从长远来看，账单最终会到期，总得有人想办法支付。

sentences.en: I mean, it sounds almost like he's bribing people to vote for him.
sentences.zh: 听起来他简直是在贿赂选民。

sentences.en: Well, that's certainly what his opponents would say.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他的反对者肯定会这么说。

sentences.en: And all of this is building towards last weekend when we had the election.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都指向了上周末的选举。

sentences.en: And what an election.
sentences.zh: 那真是一场选举。

sentences.en: It was such a nail-biter.
sentences.zh: 真是让人揪心。

sentences.en: I mean, I was watching it all day thinking, oh my God, what's going to happen?
sentences.zh: 我整天都在看，心想，天哪，会发生什么？

sentences.en: And it was so close.
sentences.zh: 而且差距太小了。

sentences.en: It was incredibly close.
sentences.zh: 差距极其微小。

sentences.en: First thing, we had tremendous turnout.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们的投票率非常高。

sentences.en: The participation rate was close to 90%.
sentences.zh: 参与率接近90%。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Just off the charts.
sentences.zh: 简直高得离谱。

sentences.en: Huge, huge numbers of people went out to vote.
sentences.zh: 大量的人出来投票。

sentences.en: So at the polling places, you just saw long lines.
sentences.zh: 在投票站，你看到排着长队。

sentences.en: You saw people excited about their particular candidates, waving flags, wearing t-shirts, all really excited to be participating in this political act.
sentences.zh: 你看到人们为自己支持的候选人感到兴奋，挥舞旗帜，穿着T恤，都非常高兴能参与到这个政治行为中来。

sentences.en: And the polls close.
sentences.zh: 投票结束了。

sentences.en: And we finally get the results, which is that Erdogan doesn't get it across the line.
sentences.zh: 我们终于得到了结果，埃尔多安没有直接胜出。

sentences.en: He ends up with 49.5%.
sentences.zh: 他最终获得了49.5%的选票。

sentences.en: So a half percent short of an outright victory.
sentences.zh: 距离直接获胜还差0.5%。

sentences.en: Kalic Staroli comes through with 44.9%.
sentences.zh: 克勒奇达尔奥卢获得了44.9%。

sentences.en: So trailing his challenger.
sentences.zh: 落后于他的挑战者。

sentences.en: And what do you make of those results?
sentences.zh: 你如何看待这些结果？

sentences.en: Well, the immediate effect is that we're going to go to a runoff.
sentences.zh: 嗯，直接的影响是我们必须进入第二轮投票。

sentences.en: On May 28th, the top two contenders, Erdogan and Kalic Starolu, are going to face off to determine who finally wins.
sentences.zh: 5月28日，排名前两位的竞争者埃尔多安和克勒奇达尔奥卢将进行对决，以决定谁最终获胜。

sentences.en: What's interesting here is that Erdogan's actually in a very strong position.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，埃尔多安实际上处于非常有利的地位。

sentences.en: There was a third candidate in the race who got about 5.2% of the vote.
sentences.zh: 竞选中还有第三位候选人，他获得了约5.2%的选票。

sentences.en: He's eliminated.
sentences.zh: 他被淘汰了。

sentences.en: And most of his voters are likely to vote for Erdogan in the second round, which could be enough to give him the victory.
sentences.zh: 他的大部分选民很可能会在第二轮投票给埃尔多安，这可能足以让他获胜。

sentences.en: And I think everybody got a sense of where this seemed to be heading the night of, after the results had come in.
sentences.zh: 我想在结果出来的那天晚上，每个人都感觉到事情的发展方向了。

sentences.en: In the middle of the night, Erdogan appears on the balcony.
sentences.zh: 半夜，埃尔多安出现在阳台上。

sentences.en: And it's dark out, and he's wearing this long black coat, and he has crowds of people beneath him who've been waiting to see if he's going to win the election.
sentences.zh: 天很黑，他穿着一件长长的黑色外套，下面聚集着等待看他是否赢得选举的人群。

sentences.en: And he comes out, standing straight up, looking very confident, and he addresses them.
sentences.zh: 他走出来，站得笔直，看起来非常自信，并向他们发表讲话。

sentences.en: And he basically says,
sentences.zh: 他基本上说，

sentences.en: We love you a lot.
sentences.zh: 我们非常爱你们。

sentences.en: This here is the result of that love.
sentences.zh: 这就是那份爱的结果。

sentences.en: In a barbed sort of jab at his opponent, he says,
sentences.zh: 在对他对手的一番带刺的嘲讽中，他说，

sentences.en: Some are in the kitchen, we are on the balcony.
sentences.zh: 有人在厨房，我们在阳台。

sentences.en: And he says, while the final results are not clear yet,
sentences.zh: 他说，虽然最终结果还不清楚，

sentences.en: We are ahead by far.
sentences.zh: 但我们遥遥领先。

sentences.en: And that seemed to show that he was confident that he was going to win.
sentences.zh: 这似乎表明他对自己获胜充满信心。

sentences.en: So there you have it.
sentences.zh: 所以，情况就是这样。

sentences.en: An unbelievable story of political survival, right?
sentences.zh: 一个令人难以置信的政治生存故事，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, years of economic turmoil, 80% inflation.
sentences.zh: 多年的经济动荡，80%的通货膨胀。

sentences.en: Like, that would spell the end for pretty much any political leader's career in a democracy, but not his.
sentences.zh: 这在民主国家的任何政治领导人身上都意味着职业生涯的终结，但他没有。

sentences.en: How do you explain that?
sentences.zh: 你如何解释这一点？

sentences.en: Turkey is a very complicated place.
sentences.zh: 土耳其是一个非常复杂的地方。

sentences.en: This is a country that people will tell you is not fully a democracy and is not fully an autocracy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个人们会告诉你既不是完全的民主国家，也不是完全的独裁国家的国家。

sentences.en: It's a hybrid.
sentences.zh: 它是一个混合体。

sentences.en: It's somewhere in this murky middle that has characteristics of both systeMs.
sentences.zh: 它处于这种模糊的中间地带，兼具两种体系的特征。

sentences.en: And because of the way this election was run, it was free.
sentences.zh: 由于这次选举的运作方式，它是自由的。

sentences.en: But because of the way that Erdogan was able to use his power to tilt the playing field in his direction beforehand, it was not really fair.
sentences.zh: 但由于埃尔多安能够利用他的权力事先向有利于他的方向倾斜竞争环境，它并不真正公平。

sentences.en: So free, but not so fair.
sentences.zh: 所以是自由的，但不太公平。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So that leaves us in a situation where he's still the survivor.
sentences.zh: 这让我们处于一种他仍然是幸存者的境地。

sentences.en: However, he's managed to do it yet again, and he's in a very good position going into this runoff on May 28th.
sentences.zh: 然而，他再次做到了，并且在5月28日的第二轮投票中处于非常有利的地位。

sentences.en: And if he wins there, he's going to have five more years to leave his mark on Turkey.
sentences.zh: 如果他在那里获胜，他将还有五年时间在土耳其留下他的印记。

sentences.en: Ben, thank you.
sentences.zh: 本，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是维娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一——《Connections》。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我热爱恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天负责创作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像刚才那两位一样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 请访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是您今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, a high-stakes meeting between President Biden and congressional leaders over the debt limit ended with leaders saying that both sides were still, quote, far apart.
sentences.zh: 周二，拜登总统与国会领导人就债务上限问题举行了一场高风险会议，会议结束时，双方领导人表示，彼此的立场仍然“相去甚远”。

sentences.en: If the debt ceiling is not lifted, the government could run out of money by June 1St.
sentences.zh: 如果债务上限不提高，政府可能会在6月1日耗尽资金。

sentences.en: But the meeting was not without some progress.
sentences.zh: 但会议并非毫无进展。

sentences.en: Speaker of the House Kevin McCarthy told reporters that it might be possible to reach a deal by the end of the week.
sentences.zh: 众议院议长凯文·麦卡锡告诉记者，本周末前达成协议是有可能的。

sentences.en: And in North Carolina, legislation banning most abortions after 12 weeks of pregnancy would become law
sentences.zh: 在北卡罗来纳州，一项禁止怀孕12周后进行大多数堕胎手术的法案即将成为法律，

sentences.en: after the state's Republican-controlled legislature successfully overrode the veto of the Democratic governor.
sentences.zh: 此前该州共和党控制的立法机构成功推翻了民主党州长的否决。

sentences.en: The override, which was completed Tuesday night, was possible because a Democrat, Tricia Cawtham,
sentences.zh: 这次推翻否决的行动于周二晚间完成，之所以能够成功，是因为一位民主党人特里西娅·考瑟姆，

sentences.en: switched parties, giving Republicans in the House the three-fifths majority needed to succeed.
sentences.zh: 转投了党派，使共和党在众议院获得了成功所需的五分之三多数席位。

sentences.en: Until now, North Carolina had allowed abortions up to 20 weeks and had become a destination in the South for women seeking abortions after Roe fell last year.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，北卡罗来纳州允许在怀孕20周前进行堕胎，并已成为去年“罗诉韦德案”被推翻后，南方女性寻求堕胎的目的地。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko, Rochelle Banja, Michael Simon-Johnson, and Astha Chattervedi.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗伯·齐普科、罗谢尔·班贾、迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊和阿斯塔·查特维迪制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Chow and Rachel Quester.
sentences.zh: 由丽莎·周和雷切尔·奎斯特编辑。

sentences.zh: 包含塞达·奥斯特鲁克和埃利夫·英格的翻译。

sentences.en: Original music by Diane Wong and Marian Lozano.
sentences.zh: 原创音乐由黛安·王和玛丽安·洛萨诺创作。

sentences.en: And was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由克里斯·伍德进行工程制作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Elif Inge.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢埃利夫·英格。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《Metro》节目中，我，莎拉·凯尼格，将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《Metro》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在您获取播客的任何平台收听。
